summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage V chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening lower extremity edema and 12-pound weight gain despite optimized diuretic therapy. He was started on IV furosemide, received two units of packed red blood cells for anemia, and was initiated on hemodialysis after placement of a tunneled dialysis catheter. He completed three dialysis sessions, lost 22 pounds, and showed improvement in renal function and volume status. His C. difficile infection was managed with a tapering course of oral vancomycin, and vitamin D deficiency was addressed with weekly supplementation. He was discharged home with services, continuing dialysis, diuretics, and close follow-up.
